## Summary

Lear Corporation is a US automotive supplier headquartered in
Southfield, Michigan, founded in Detroit in 1917 as American Metal
Products and listed on the NYSE as LEA [1]. Its two businesses are
Seating and E-Systems, the latter making vehicle wiring, connectors and
electronic controllers [1]. Lear's E-Systems page lists wire harnesses,
connection systems, high- and low-voltage power distribution including
a battery disconnect unit, and zonal and body domain controllers such
as its Zone Control Module [2].

The IEEE registry lists five MA-L blocks to "LEAR" at Industriestrasse
48 in Kronach, Germany and Carrer Fuster 54 in Valls, Spain, two to
"Lear Corporation GmbH" and one to "Lear Corporation", all three
spellings sharing the Kronach address [3]. A MAC from these blocks is
most plausibly a vehicle electronic module, but no source consulted
names the product or its radios, so those fields are left empty [2][3].
An NVD keyword search for Lear Corporation returned only an unrelated
Learn2 Corporation entry, so no security note is recorded [4]. The FCC
ID databases refused the session that wrote this entry, so no grantee
code or silicon is listed.
